author: MinuteEarth
description:
Way back at the dawn of aviation, during a public flight exhibition of all things, a gull jammed a plane’s controls, crashing the plane and killing the pilot. Today, there are thousands of commercial airliners – and billions of birds – in the sky at any given time, so it seems like they should run into each other all the time. So why don’t birds cause more plane crashes?

LEARN MORE
**************
To learn more about this topic, start your googling with these keywords: 
- Aviation: The design, manufacture, and operation of aircraft — and, more broadly, the practice of mechanical flight itself, from a single-seat glider to a transcontinental airliner.
- Shrapnel: Fragments scattered by the explosion of a shell, bomb, or mine; loosely, any of the broken pieces thrown off by a violent blast.
